name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,342

entries.clue: Mafiosi — or magi? (4,4)

blocks.note: American slang for members of the Mafia
the Magi are the three wise men of the Nativity, read jokingly

annotation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a gang of mobsters might be the three kings.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: the Magi are literally wise men, so 'wise guys' fits them as well as it fits gangsters.
annotation.definitionFit: Wiseguy is American slang for a Mafia member, and the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity.

entries.clue: Trimmed boot skilfully (4)

indicatorNotes.Trimmed: trimming cuts the end off a word

blocks.note: WELLY, a rubber boot, loses its last letter Y

annotation.surface: A boot that has been neatly cut down by a skilled hand.
annotation.walkthrough: A welly is a wellington, the British name for a rubber rain boot.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adverb synonym: a job done well is one done with skill.

entries.clue: Angrily snarled disparaging words (7)

annotation.surface: Someone snarling insults in a temper.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is so close in meaning to the answer that the surface reads as a plain description of slander.
annotation.definitionFit: Slander is false spoken words that damage someone's reputation.

entries.clue: Snitch on American painter, chirpy six-footer (11)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, A on B puts A above B

blocks.note: to grass is British slang for to inform on someone

annotation.surface: An informer betraying an American artist, followed by a cheery tall man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it means an insect with six legs that chirps.
annotation.definitionFit: A grasshopper is a six-legged insect known for its chirping.

entries.clue: Fret about eating a herb (6)

indicatorNotes.about: turning about sends the word backwards
indicatorNotes.eating: the outer word takes the A inside it

blocks.note: the letter A, placed inside YRROW

annotation.surface: Someone anxious about swallowing some herbal remedy.
annotation.walkthrough: WORRY turned round is YRROW, which then swallows the A after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a feathery-leaved herb used in folk medicine.

entries.clue: Reportedly slope away and come together (4)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: what is reported is heard, not read

blocks.note: ground that sinks slopes away downwards

annotation.surface: A rumour that land is subsiding and joining up.
annotation.walkthrough: SINK and SYNC are pronounced the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Things that sync come together in time, as sound with picture.

entries.clue: Enemy destroyed SW Asian country (5)

indicatorNotes.destroyed: a destroyed word is broken into its letters

annotation.surface: A foe that wrecked a nation in the Middle East.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as war news, which hides that 'destroyed' only rearranges ENEMY.
annotation.definitionFit: Yemen lies at the southwest corner of the Arabian peninsula.

entries.clue: Censures Conservative and Democrat, extremely nefarious (8)

indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of NefariouS

annotation.surface: A politician rebukes both parties as thoroughly wicked.
annotation.walkthrough: The political surface makes CON and DEM look like part of the story rather than standard abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: To condemn is to censure, to express strong disapproval.

entries.clue: Climber in Australian Alps (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits in the words that follow

annotation.surface: A mountaineer in the Australian Alps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, which the Alps encourage; it is a climbing plant.
annotation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests.

entries.clue: Setter’s introduced to new “green” course of treatment (7)

indicatorNotes.introduced to: one piece is put inside another
indicatorNotes.new: a new version of GREEN has its letters rearranged

blocks.note: setter's = I'm, the setter speaking of himself

annotation.surface: The puzzle-maker being put on a new eco-friendly health plan.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotes around 'green' make it look like eco-jargon; it is only letters to rearrange, with IM placed inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of medical treatment, diet or exercise.

entries.clue: Instruction to codebreaker? “Look lively!” (3,8)

blocks.note: a codebreaker's job is to crack codes
both mean hurry up and start

annotation.surface: A boss urging a cipher expert to hurry up.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the first definition as a literal reading of the idiom.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Get cracking!' means get moving; read literally it tells a codebreaker to crack.

entries.clue: Put a stop to seduction in Barking (11)

indicatorNotes.Barking: barking means mad, so the letters go crazy

annotation.surface: Ending a seduction taking place in Barking, a district of East London.
annotation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the London district, and 'in' like a preposition; barking is British slang for mad, and 'in' is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: discontinuing a product or service means ending it for good.

entries.clue: On the way out, boy cashes in his chips (6,2)

blocks.note: passé = outdated, going out of fashion

annotation.surface: A young man leaving a casino and turning his chips into money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cashes in his chips' sounds like a gambler leaving the table; it is an idiom for dying.
annotation.definitionFit: To cash in one's chips and to pass on are both euphemisms for dying.

entries.clue: Display prisoner in cooler (3,3)

blocks.note: to air views is to display them

annotation.surface: A jail putting an inmate on show in the cells.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is slang for jail, which the prisoner seems to confirm; here it means an air conditioner.
annotation.definitionFit: Air con is short for air conditioning, which cools a room.

entries.clue: Guttersnipe stumbling about naked (6)

indicatorNotes.naked: a naked word is stripped of its outer letters

blocks.note: LURCHING (stumbling about) loses its outer letters L and G

annotation.surface: A street child staggering around with no clothes on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Naked' fits the picture of a ragged child, but it tells you to strip the covering letters from LURCHING.
annotation.definitionFit: A guttersnipe is a scruffy child of the streets, an urchin.

entries.clue: Fairly tough detective trapped in grating (7)

indicatorNotes.trapped in: one piece is caught inside another

annotation.surface: A hard-nosed detective stuck in a drain grating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grating' looks like a metal grille that could trap someone; it is the adjective meaning harsh.
annotation.definitionFit: Hardish means somewhat hard, fairly tough.

entries.clue: Kind of Blue’s energy topped by much of non-commercial music (6)

indicatorNotes.topped by: in a down clue the second piece sits on top of the first
indicatorNotes.much of: most of the word, without its last letter

blocks.note: INDIE music loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A jazz critic on Miles Davis's album Kind of Blue and its debt to underground music.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics make 'Kind of Blue' a Miles Davis album title, but read plainly it defines a shade of blue. The 's means 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: indigo is one variety of blue, the dark dye of the indigo plant.

entries.clue: Kipper transporter? (8,3)

blocks.note: the surface wants a smoked herring; the setter means someone having a kip, a sleeper
the surface wants a fish lorry; the setter means a railway carriage carrying such passengers

annotation.surface: A lorry carrying smoked herrings.
annotation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring, and kip is British slang for sleep; the clue takes a kipper to mean a sleeper.
annotation.definitionFit: A sleeping car is a railway carriage with beds that carries sleeping passengers.

entries.clue: TV honours some of them, mystifyingly (5)

indicatorNotes.some of: only part of the following words is used

annotation.surface: A puzzled viewer remarks that the awards go to some of those nominees for no clear reason.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mystifyingly' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters sit in order across the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: The Emmys are the American awards for excellence in television.

entries.clue: Cases of completely stagnant growth (4)

indicatorNotes.Cases of: the case of a word is its outside, first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of CompletelY
first and last letters of StagnanT

annotation.surface: Examples of a business stuck with zero growth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stagnant growth' reads as flat economics, and 'Cases' as instances; the cases are the outer letters of the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A cyst is an abnormal growth, a sac in the body.

entries.clue: You’re adopted by nomadic Masai warrior caste (7)

annotation.surface: A reader being taken in by the wandering Masai people of East Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nomadic' describes the Masai truthfully, which hides that it rearranges their name.
annotation.definitionFit: The samurai were the hereditary military caste of feudal Japan.

entries.clue: First to leave island without warmth (5)

indicatorNotes.First to leave: the first letter of the word is the one that departs, as the first guest to leave a party

blocks.note: SICILY loses its first letter S

annotation.surface: The first person to depart an island in winter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without warmth' seems to describe leaving a cold island, but it is the definition, an adverb.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: an icy manner is cold and unfriendly, so to speak icily is to speak without warmth.

entries.clue: Periodically insensate in hideout (4)

indicatorNotes.Periodically: at regular intervals, every other letter

annotation.surface: Someone lying numb from time to time in a hiding place.
annotation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'insensate' spell the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An extended sense: a bird's nest is its refuge, so a nest is also a secluded retreat, as in a thieves' nest.

entries.clue: Outsider yearns to finally push back (4,4)

indicatorNotes.finally: what comes finally in a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.back: the pieces are turned back to front

annotation.surface: An underdog who wants to shove back against the favourites.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Push back' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'back' only reverses the letters before it. An outsider is a horse or candidate given little chance.
annotation.definitionFit: An outsider is a runner not expected to win, a long shot.
